title: Localization at the unique prime over a base prime
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module via $\varphi$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be a prime ideal, and let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be the unique prime ideal satisfying $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. Put $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and use localizations as in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The canonical $B$-algebra homomorphism $S^{-1}B\to B_{\mathfrak q}$, $b/s\mapsto b/\varphi(s)$, is an isomorphism. For every $B$-module $M$, its induced map $M\otimes_A A_{\mathfrak p}\to M_{\mathfrak q}$, $m\otimes(a/s)\mapsto\varphi(a)m/\varphi(s)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], is an $A_{\mathfrak p}$-linear isomorphism, natural in $M$.

source.place: Tag 00EA (algebra-lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below), case (1)+(2)(a) specialized to a finite ring map; module consequence by localization of scalars.

proof.text: By the finite-module hypothesis, the ring map $\varphi:A\to B$ is integral (every element of $B$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$). If $\mathfrak q'\subset B$ lies over a prime $\mathfrak p'\subseteq\mathfrak p$, going-up produces a prime $\mathfrak q''\supseteq\mathfrak q'$ lying over $\mathfrak p$; the assumed uniqueness of the prime over $\mathfrak p$ gives $\mathfrak q''=\mathfrak q$. Hence every prime of $B$ whose contraction is contained in $\mathfrak p$ is contained in $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 00EA (lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below), finite-map specialization of going-up case (1)+(2)(a).

proof.text: Let $\lambda:B\to S^{-1}B$ be the localization map at the image of $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$, and let $\mathfrak q_S=\mathfrak q(S^{-1}B)$. The arbitrary-localization prime correspondence identifies the primes of $S^{-1}B$ with primes $\mathfrak q'\subset B$ disjoint from $\varphi(S)$; their contractions $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$ are contained in $\mathfrak p$, so Step 1 gives $\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak q$ and therefore every prime of $S^{-1}B$ is contained in $\mathfrak q_S$. If an element outside $\mathfrak q_S$ were not a unit, its principal ideal would lie in a maximal (hence prime) ideal, contradicting this containment. Thus every element outside $\mathfrak q_S$ is already invertible in $S^{-1}B$, so $(S^{-1}B)_{\mathfrak q_S}=S^{-1}B$.

source.place: Tag 00EA (lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below), final paragraph, with the maximal-ideal argument expanded.

proof.text: Apply the localization-at-a-prime clause of the arbitrary-localization node to $\lambda$ and $\mathfrak q_S$. It gives an isomorphism $B_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}(S^{-1}B)_{\mathfrak q_S}$ sending $b/t$ to $\lambda(b)/\lambda(t)$. Using Step 2 to identify the target with $S^{-1}B$, its inverse is the canonical $B$-algebra map $S^{-1}B\to B_{\mathfrak q}$, $b/s\mapsto b/\varphi(s)$, and is therefore an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00EA (lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below), conclusion via the canonical localization maps.

proof.text: Restrict $M$ along $\varphi$ to an $A$-module. Apply localization commuting with tensor over the base with both rings equal to $A$, its module $A$, multiplicative subset $S$, and other module $M$. Using the elementary tensor unit $A\otimes_A M\cong M$ and tensor symmetry, this gives $M\otimes_AA_{\mathfrak p}\cong S^{-1}M$, with map $m\otimes(a/s)\mapsto\varphi(a)m/s$ (the unit map is $a\otimes m\mapsto\varphi(a)m$, inverse $m\mapsto1\otimes m$). Next, in the $S^{-1}B$-module $S^{-1}M$, every $b\notin\mathfrak q$ acts invertibly by Step 3. Define $M_{\mathfrak q}\to S^{-1}M$ by $m/b\mapsto (b/1)^{-1}(m/1)$. If $m/b=m^{\prime}/b^{\prime}$, some $t\notin\mathfrak q$ kills $b^{\prime}m-bm^{\prime}$, so the invertibility of $t,b,b^{\prime}$ proves equality of the images. This is inverse to $S^{-1}M\to M_{\mathfrak q}$, $m/s\mapsto m/\varphi(s)$, by the same fraction relations. Thus the required module isomorphism follows.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), followed by the elementary change of denominators from Tag 00EA.

proof.text: Composing the two displayed maps sends $m\otimes(a/s)$ to $\varphi(a)m/\varphi(s)$, exactly the map in the statement. Both maps respect the $A_{\mathfrak p}$-action, and the fraction formulas commute with every $B$-linear map $M\to M'$, proving $A_{\mathfrak p}$-linearity and naturality.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), displayed fraction formula and its compatibility with module maps.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00EA, using Tag 00DK for the module tensor consequence and the localization prime correspondence in the cited general localization lemma.

lean.statement: theorem uniquePrimeLocalization {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B] (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime] (hpq : Ideal.comap (algebraMap A B) q = p) (huniq : ∀ (q' : Ideal B), q'.IsPrime → Ideal.comap (algebraMap A B) q' = p → q' = q) : Function.Bijective (uniquePrimeLocalizationMap p q hpq) ∧ ∃ e : ∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower A B M], UniquePrimeModuleEquiv p q hpq M, (∀ (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [Module A M] [IsScalarTower A B M] (m : M) (a : A) (s : p.primeCompl), e M (m ⊗ₜ[A] IsLocalization.mk' (Localization.AtPrime p) a s) = LocalizedModule.mk (algebraMap A B a • m) (⟨algebraMap A B s, fun h ↦ s.property ((congrArg (fun I : Ideal A ↦ (s : A) ∈ I) hpq).mp h)⟩ : q.primeCompl)) ∧ (∀ (M N : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B M] [Module B N] [Module A M] [Module A N] [IsScalarTower A B M] [IsScalarTower A B N] (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (x : M ⊗[A] Localization.AtPrime p), e N ((f.restrictScalars A).rTensor (Localization.AtPrime p) x) = LocalizedModule.map q.primeCompl f (e M x))
